_readme: Every reward, price and shop rule lives here. Edit numbers, save, reload the game. The game reads 'rewards', 'events' and 'shop'. All shop items below are PLACEHOLDER test data - names, prices and effects are just there so the shop has something to show (effects are not applied yet). See docs/ECONOMY.md for what every field means, and run 'py tools/economy_report.py' for a quick balance table.

rewards._note: The base coins for hitting each window come from the projectile in use - see 'projectiles' below (rewards.W20 / rewards.W21). The streak is only a counter now: it adds no coins.

_aimNote: Speed of the two aim markers (offset and strength - always the same, fixed speed). markerHz = full back-and-forth sweeps per second (1.275 = one sweep in ~0.8s; it was 0.85 = ~1.2s). Nothing changes it: not the streak, not buffs, not the projectile. offsetZoneAtWeight100 = the share of the OFFSET slider that is a guaranteed W20 hit for a weight-100 projectile (the snowball): 0.5 = half the slider. A weight of 0 always needs the exact middle (share 0), a weight of 200 hits anywhere (share 1), and every other weight is on a straight line through these three points. Lower it to make the snowball offset harder - note that with 0.5 the snowball offset slider only spans +-0.31 swing, which is too short to reach W21 (it needs about +-0.37).
_rarityNote: Every projectile (in "projectiles") and every buff (in the shop items) has a rarity number, bigger = rarer: the PROJECTILES and BUFFS tabs list the rarest first (equal rarities: projectiles by W20 hit value, buffs in file order). The numbers are PLACEHOLDERS - 1, 2, 3 in the current order - to be decided later.
_weightTiersNote: PROJECTILE WEIGHT is a tier, not a number. A tier is where on the STRENGTH slider a throw of that projectile lands in W20: from-to are shares of the slider (0 = its start, 1 = its tip) - very light 0-25%, light 25-50%, moderate 37.5-62.5%, heavy 50-75%, very heavy 75-100%. Every band is 25% wide, so the strength part is equally easy for all tiers; only where it is differs. The tier also sets how wide the OFFSET slider is (lighter = a wider, less precise swing): it uses the old weight number equal to the middle of the band (25 / 75 / 100 / 125 / 175). label is the word on the projectile's card. A projectile names its tier in projectiles.<id>.weight.
_raritiesNote: Rarities, from the lowest to the rarest. projectileHitValue: what ONE HIT pays (base coins, before buffs and events) with a projectile of this rarity - the same for both goal windows and for every projectile of the rarity: default (the snowball) 4, common 16, rare 128, epic 960, legendary 4800 (a standard stack is 3-7 pieces at a price per piece 8 / 60 / 450 / 2250 up to 12 / 100 / 750 / 3750, average 10 / 80 / 600 / 3000, so the hit value is always above the highest price; a stack costs 50 / 400 / 3000 / 15000 on average). A projectile can override it with its own hitValue - the HEAVY HITTERS do (Stone 40, Egg 320, Grenade 2400): a smaller stack (1-3 instead of 3-7), a price per piece 2.5x higher and a hit value 2.5x higher, for the same average stack price - higher risk, higher reward. availabilitySeconds: how long an item of that rarity stays on sale in the shop before its slot REROLLS (a new item, amount and price) - 30 min for every rarity (better rarity no longer means longer); the timer is shown on the card and runs on the device clock (also while the app is closed); a rarity without it (default) has no timer. default (light grey, chance 0) is the snowball's: it can never come up in the shop. For the others a shop slot first rolls a rarity by chance (percent - only rarities that have an item to sell take part, and their chances are rescaled to 100), then picks one of that rarity's items at random. color is CSS text colour, or rainbow (animated waves + a pulsing shine). Every projectile (in projectiles) and every shop item names one with rarity; the PROJECTILES and BUFFS tabs list the rarest first and an item with NO rarity always goes at the very end, after default and common.
_projectilesNote: Gameplay settings for every projectile you can equip (the id must match its shop item / its entry in the PROJECTILES list). regen { max, everySeconds }: a refilling stock (the snowball): the player starts with max, every one thrown is given back at one per everySeconds (by the device clock, also while the app is closed), and its card never leaves the list even at 0. infinite: true = never runs out (none right now). Every other projectile is a CONSUMABLE: one is used up the moment the player taps TAP to aim, and it is NOT given back if the aim is abandoned; when the last one is gone the snowball is equipped again. rarity: its tier - it decides the HIT VALUE (see rarities.projectileHitValue). weight: the WEIGHT TIER (see weightTiers): where on the strength slider it hits W20 and how wide the offset slider is. Shown to the player as the tier word. leavesMark: false = no snow mark, it bounces off instead. spins: it rotates in flight.

shop._priceOverrideNote: PLACEHOLDER: while priceOverride is a number, EVERY item costs that many coins in the shop (so we can test buying). Set it to null to use each item's real 'price' below.
shop._restockNote: After buying, that slot shows SOLD OUT for this many seconds (by the device clock, so it also counts while the app is closed), then restocks. 1800 = 30 minutes (60 = 1 minute is handy for testing; 3600 = 1 hour).
shop._buffMaxNote: Optional: the most copies of ONE buff the player can hold; buying one they are already maxed on is refused like too little money (the card shakes, nothing is charged). Not set now = no limit. Add "buffMax": 99 to bring the old cap back.
shop._itemsNote: Empty slots show (TBD) - the shop only has real items now. Optional item field image = a picture path for the card. Consumables are timed BUFFS: bought = active right away for duration.seconds, with a list of effects (guideLines, precision, strengthControl, coinMultiplier - see src/buffs.js). a single item can have priceRange {min, max} instead of price: its price is rolled in that range each time it is put on sale. category is 'consumable' (a timed buff: can be on sale in several slots at once; needs a duration) or 'projectile' (a stack of consumable projectiles: each time it is put on sale the amount (amount.min..max) and the price of ONE (unitPrice.min..max) are rolled at random, the slot's price is amount x unitPrice; the same stack can be on sale in several slots at once, each with its own roll).
